Below is a structured, progressive 12-week strength program designed for a beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. It focuses on full-body strength using bodyweight progressions, smart volume increases, and sufficient recovery. The plan is split into phases, with clear week-by-week structure, exercise progressions, sets/reps, tempo, rest, and optional conditioning. Basic nutrition and recovery guidelines are included at the end.

Overview
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Optional short conditioning on one or two non-lifting days.
- Session length: 40–60 minutes.
- Warm-up every session: 5–8 min (see template).
- Tempo notation: e.g., 3-1-1 = 3s lower, 1s pause, 1s up.
- Rest between sets: 60–120s for large movements; 45–90s for accessory/core.
- Progression: volume and difficulty progress across phases; deloads and testing included.

Movement Library (primary progressions)
- Pulling (bar): Assisted chin-up/pull-up (chair or slow negative), flexed-arm hang, scapular pull-ups, isometric holds, full chin-up/pull-up.
- Pushing (floor/wall): Wall push-up → incline push-up (hands on countertop/sofa) → knee push-up → full push-up → tempo/deficit/feet-elevated.
- Squat pattern: Supported sit-to-stand → bodyweight squat → tempo squat → pause squat → split squat → Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on chair/sofa).
- Hinge pattern: Hip bridge → glute bridge (single-leg progression) → hip thrust (shoulders on sofa) → hamstring walkouts.
- Core/anti-extension: Dead bug, hollow hold/hollow rock progression, plank/RKC plank, side plank.
- Upper back/shoulders: Pike scapular shrugs, pike/elevated pike push-up progression, Y-T-W prone raises (no load), reverse snow angels.
- Posterior chain/isometrics: Iso hamstring curls (heel slides on towel), Nordic eccentric (improv with knees on mat, feet wedged under sofa if possible).

Weekly Warm-up Template (5–8 min)
- Joint prep: Neck circles x5 each, shoulder CARs x5 each, hip CARs x3 each.
- Dynamic: Leg swings x10 each, arm circles x10 each, inchworms x5, hip hinge drill x10.
- Activation: Scapular pull-ups x6–8, glute bridge x12, dead bug x6/side.

Cool-down (3–5 min)
- Easy nasal breathing, 90/90 hip stretch, doorway chest stretch, child’s pose or thoracic rotations.

Phase 1: Foundations and Movement Quality (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Learn patterns, build base strength and joint tolerance, establish tempo control.

Week 1 (3 sessions)
Session A
- Squat to box/chair: 3x10, 3-1-1, rest 60–90s
- Incline push-up (hands on counter/sofa): 4x6–8, 3-1-1, rest 90s
- Assisted chin-up (feet on chair) or slow negatives: 5x3 negatives (4–5s down) or 4x6 assisted reps, rest 90–120s
- Hip bridge: 3x12–15, 2-1-2
- Dead bug: 3x6/side slow
- Scapular pull-ups: 2x8–10

Session B
- Split squat (hands lightly on wall for balance): 3x8/leg, 3-1-1
- Knee push-up: 4x8–10, 2-1-1
- Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar): 4x max hold (10–20s target), rest 90–120s; if not possible, 4x3–4 eccentric chin-ups
- Hip thrust (shoulders on sofa): 3x10–12, 2-1-2
- Side plank: 3x20–30s/side
- Reverse snow angels (prone): 2x10–12

Session C
- Tempo bodyweight squat: 4x8, 4-1-1
- Incline push-up: 4x8–10, 2-1-1 (lower hand height if >10 easy)
- Assisted neutral-grip chin-up (towel over bar for neutral grip if desired): 5x3–4 negatives or 4x6 assisted
- Hamstring walkouts (from bridge): 3x6–8 slow
- Hollow hold: 4x15–25s (regress to tuck as needed)
- Pike scapular shrugs: 2x10–12

Week 2
- Progress each main lift by 1–2 reps/set or add a set if all sets hit top reps with 1–2 RIR (reps in reserve).
- Introduce brief isometric pauses: add 1s pause at bottom of squats and push-ups.
- Pulling: Aim to extend negative chin-ups to 5–6s; add 1–2 flexed-arm hang seconds per set.

Week 3
- Raise difficulty slightly:
  - Push-ups: lower hand height or switch half the sets to full push-ups if ready (sets of 4–6).
  - Squats: add 1–2 reps/set; option to progress to pause squats (2s).
  - Chin-ups: combine 1–2 assisted concentric reps followed by 1–2 slow negatives per set.
- Core: Hollow hold 20–35s; side plank 30–40s.

Optional Conditioning (Weeks 1–3, 1–2x/week, 10–15 min)
- EMOM 10: 6–8 incline or knee push-ups (min 1), 8–10 squats (min 2). Keep 2–3 RIR.

Phase 2: Progressive Strength and Skill Acquisition (Weeks 4–7)
Goal: Transition to harder variations, increase pulling capacity, build unilateral lower body strength.

Week 4
Session A
- Pause squat (2s): 4x8
- Full push-up (or mixed sets with knee): 5x5–8, 3-1-1
- Chin-up cluster: 6 rounds of 1 assisted concentric + 1 slow negative (5–6s), rest 60–75s between rounds
- Hip thrust (sofa): 4x10–12; last set AMRAP leaving 1–2 RIR
- Hollow hold: 4x25–35s
- Scapular pull-ups: 2x10–12

Session B
- Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa): 4x6–8/leg, 3-1-1
- Pike push-up (hips high; hands on floor, feet on mat): 4x6–8; regress to incline if needed
- Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar): 5x max hold; supinated or neutral grip; aim 15–25s
- Hamstring walkouts: 4x6–10
- Side plank with top-leg raise (if able): 3x20–30s/side
- Reverse snow angels: 2x12–15

Session C
- Tempo squat: 4x8 (4-0-1) or add 1–2 jump squats x3 sets of 5 (submaximal, focus on crisp takeoff/soft landing)
- Push-up: 5x6–10; elevate feet 10–20 cm if regular >10 easy
- Assisted chin-up density: 8 min “every 45–60s” do 1–2 concentric assisted reps + 1 negative
- Single-leg glute bridge: 3x10–12/leg
- Hollow rocks or dead bug contralateral reach: 3x10–12
- Pike scap shrugs: 2x12–15

Week 5
- Add 1 set to squats and push-ups if all sets left ≥2 RIR.
- Chin-up work: extend negatives to 6–7s; start trying single unassisted eccentric initiations if safe.
- Bulgarian split squat: aim 8–10 reps/leg across 4 sets.
- Core holds +5–10s.

Week 6
- Push: incorporate feet-elevated push-ups for top sets: 2–3 sets x 5–8; back-off sets standard push-ups x8–12.
- Pull: Introduce isometric mid-range hold: chin-up negatives with 3s hold at 90° elbow flexion. 4–5 sets x 1–2 reps.
- Squat: Pause split squat 2s at bottom for 3 sets.
- Hinge: Hip thrust last set AMRAP (stop 1 RIR).

Week 7
- Density week: Keep exercises but reduce rest slightly (by ~15–20%) while keeping reps. Alternatively, add a small EMOM finisher:
  - EMOM 8: 2–3 assisted chin-ups, 6–8 push-ups alternating minutes.

Phase 3: Consolidation, Strength Peaks, and Skill Testing (Weeks 8–12)
Goal: Solidify strength, attempt first unassisted chin-ups, harder push-up variations, stronger unilateral legs, and refine core stability.

Week 8
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat: 5x6–8/leg (2s pause bottom)
- Push-up: 5x8–12 or 4x5–8 feet-elevated + 1 back-off AMRAP (stop 1 RIR)
- Chin-up wave sets: 5–6 rounds of 1 assisted concentric + 1–2 negatives (6–8s) + max 10–20s hold
- Hip thrust (sofa): 4x12–15
- Hollow hold: 4x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat: 4x10 (4-0-1)
- Pike push-up: 5x6–10 (progress to elevated pike by placing feet on sofa if strong)
- Flexed-arm hang: 5 sets max; then scapular pull-ups 2x12–15
- Single-leg bridge: 4x12–15/leg
- Side plank: 3x30–45s/side
- Reverse snow angels: 2x15–20

Session C
- Squat + power primer: 3x10 bodyweight squat, then 3x5 jump squats (submax)
- Push-up ladder: 5x submax sets leaving 1–2 RIR; total 40–60 reps target
- Chin-up attempts: 6–8 singles—try unassisted concentric; if not yet, use minimal assistance for 1–2 reps/set; finish with 2x1 slow negative (8s)
- Hamstring walkouts: 3x10–12
- Hollow rocks: 3x12–15

Week 9
- Progress reps or elevate difficulty:
  - Feet-elevated push-ups for most sets; aim 6–10 reps.
  - Chin-up: increase attempts to 8–10 singles across session; include band/towel foot assist only as needed; negatives 8–10s.
  - Bulgarian split squat: 5x8–10/leg as able.
- Optional finisher: EMOM 10 alternating 2–3 assisted chins and 6–8 push-ups.

Week 10
- Micro-peak on pushing and legs; maintain pulling skill volume.
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat: 5x8–10/leg
- Feet-elevated push-up: 5x6–10
- Chin-up cluster: 6–8 rounds—attempt 1 unassisted; if fail, 1 assisted concentric + 1 negative (8–10s)
- Hip thrust: 4x12–15 (last set AMRAP, 1 RIR)
- Hollow hold: 4x35–45s

Session B
- Tempo squat: 4x10, 4-1-1
- Pike push-up (elevated feet if strong): 5x6–9
- Flexed-arm hang: 5x max; try to exceed 25–35s
- Single-leg bridge: 4x12–15
- Side plank with top-leg raise: 3x25–35s/side

Session C
- Squat density: 5 rounds—45s work/45s rest: steady squats at controlled pace (accumulate quality reps)
- Push-up ladder to 50–70 total reps (include feet-elevated early sets)
- Chin-up EMOM 8: 1 attempt + 1 negative each minute

Week 11 (Taper and Skill Emphasis)
- Reduce total sets by ~25%, keep intensity of key attempts.
- Two main sessions + 1 light technique session.

Session A
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x6–8/leg (quality)
- Push-up: 3x6–10 feet-elevated
- Chin-up: 6–8 singles—attempt unassisted; follow any miss with 1 negative (8–10s)
- Core: Hollow hold 3x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat: 3x8
- Pike push-up: 3x6–8
- Flexed-arm hang: 3x max
- Single-leg bridge: 3x10–12
- Side plank: 2x30–40s/side

Session C (light)
- Movement flow, mobility, 2x8–10 easy squats, 2x6–8 incline or standard push-ups, 4–6 assisted chin-up reps total. Keep fresh.

Week 12 (Test and Consolidate)
Session A (Test)
- After warm-up, test:
  - Max quality push-ups (strict, full ROM) in one set—stop 1 rep before form breaks.
  - Chin-up attempts: up to 6–8 singles; record best number of unassisted reps in a set. If none yet, record best controlled negative duration and best flexed-arm hang.
  - Bulgarian split squat AMRAP set/leg at clean tempo: stop at 1–2 RIR (cap at 20).
- Accessory: light hip thrust 2x12, core 2x30–40s.

Session B (Volume back-on)
- Squat: 4x10
- Push-up: 4x8–12 (feet-elevated as able)
- Chin-up: 6x1–2 assisted + negative focus

Session C (Skill and Capacity)
- EMOM 12: Odd minutes 2–3 chin-ups (use least assistance needed), Even minutes 6–10 push-ups (variation scaled).
- Cool-down and note progress.

Progression Rules and Cues
- Reps in reserve (RIR): Keep 1–2 RIR on most sets. If you finish all sets with >2 RIR, progress next session by +1–2 reps or harder variation. If you hit 0 RIR early, hold or regress slightly to keep quality.
- Tempo and range: Prioritize full ROM and controlled tempo over chasing reps.
- Pull-up assistance: Use minimal foot-on-chair or slight jump to get above the bar only as much as needed, then own a slow negative.

Optional Minimal Conditioning (1–2x/week, 12–18 min)
- Choose one:
  - EMOM 12: 6–10 squats, 4–8 push-ups, 20–30s plank alternating.
  - Circuit x3–4: 40s brisk step-ups on sturdy step/stairs (if available), 30s mountain climbers, 30s glute bridge, 30–45s rest.

Mobility/Recovery (daily 5–10 min)
- Thoracic extension over small pillow/rolled towel x60–90s
- Hip flexor stretch x45–60s/side
- Calf and hamstring stretch x45–60s/side
- Breathe: 3–5 min nasal 4-6 breathing post-session

Basic Nutrition Guidelines for Strength and Recovery
- Protein: ~0.7–1.0 g per lb bodyweight (1.6–2.2 g/kg) daily; distribute across 3–5 meals.
- Calories: Aim at slight surplus if muscle gain is priority (+150–300 kcal/day). If weight must be stable, maintain while prioritizing protein.
- Carbs: Include carbs pre- and post-workout (e.g., fruit + yogurt before; rice/pasta/potatoes + lean protein after).
- Hydration: 2–3 liters water/day; add 500 ml around training.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time, consistent daily.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; consistent schedule.

Safety and Setup Tips in a Small Flat
- Doorway pull-up bar: Ensure secure installation per manufacturer; test with hangs before full reps.
- For assistance: Place a sturdy chair under the bar for foot support; keep core tight to avoid swinging.
- Floor: Use yoga mat for knees/elbows; use a towel under heels for hamstring slides.
- Balance: For Bulgarians/split squats, lightly hold wall or doorframe until stable form is automatic.

Expected Outcomes by Week 12 (typical beginner, consistent adherence)
- Push-ups: From incline/knees to 10–20 solid floor push-ups; some may have 5–10 feet-elevated.
- Pull-ups: From negatives/hangs to first 1–3 unassisted chin-ups; if not yet, markedly longer hangs and slower, controlled negatives.
- Legs: Strong, stable split squat/Bulgarian sets of 8–12/leg with pauses; improved jump mechanics and hip hinge strength.
- Core: 30–45s hollow holds and strong, braced positioning under load.

Use this as the master plan; feel free to adjust weekly based on the client’s RIR feedback, recovery, and any joint sensitivities.

Here’s a simple, effective 12-week nutrition plan to support strength gains, recovery, and consistency for a beginner training at home. It’s built to be flexible, affordable, and easy to follow without tracking every gram unless you want to. Adjust portions based on progress.

Step 1: Set targets
- Calories:
  - Goal: lean muscle gain with minimal fat. Start at bodyweight (lb) x 15 kcal. If bodyweight unknown, start at 2,400–2,800 kcal/day for an average 27-year-old male. Adjust by 150–250 kcal every 1–2 weeks based on progress:
    - If average weekly weight gain <0.25% BW for 2 weeks, add +150–250 kcal/day.
    - If gaining >0.5% BW/week or feeling sluggish, reduce −150–250 kcal/day.
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g per lb BW (1.8–2.2 g/kg) daily.
- Fat: 25–35% of total calories (minimum 0.3 g/kg).
- Carbs: Fill the remainder after protein and fat. Emphasize more carbs around training.

Step 2: Simple plate method (no tracking)

  - Examples: rice + eggs/egg whites; tuna wrap + fruit; pasta + chicken + tomato sauce; protein smoothie with milk, oats, banana.

Step 5: 7-day sample menu (rotate and mix)
- Daily hydration: 2.5–3.5 L water; add 500 ml around training. Salt food to taste (especially on training days).

Day 1

Here’s a practical, low-impact home cardio plan that complements the 12-week strength program and fits a small flat with only a mat and a doorway pull-up bar. It uses minimal space, is joint-friendly, and won’t compromise strength gains.

Guiding principles
- Frequency: 2–3 cardio sessions/week on non-lifting or light days. Keep at least 6–8 hours between a hard cardio and a strength session if done same day.
- Duration: 10–25 minutes/session. Start short; progress gradually.
- Intensity: Use RPE (rate of perceived exertion) 1–10 scale.
  - Zone 2 (easy–moderate): RPE 4–6, conversational pace.
  - Tempo/threshold: RPE 7–8, sentences hard to say.
  - Intervals: RPE 8–9 on “work,” RPE 3–4 on “recover.”
- Warm-up: 3–5 minutes of joint prep and light movement before every cardio.
- Surfaces/noise: Choose low-impact options if you have downstairs neighbors; use a yoga mat or rug to soften impact.

Movement menu (mix and match)
- Low-impact steady options: brisk marching in place, step-ups on a sturdy step/stair, shadow boxing, low step-touch, single-unders with invisible rope, alternating knee drives, lateral steps, bear crawl forward/back 3–5 steps, hip hinge “good-morning” pulses.
- Moderate/high options: high-knee march or run in place, mountain climbers, skaters (low height), jumping jacks (or step-out jacks for low impact), jump rope (imaginary to reduce noise), burpee walk-outs (no jump), squat-to-calf-raise repeats.
- Conditioning accessories: doorway bar hangs or scap pull-ups between rounds to open shoulders; not during very hard intervals.

Weekly structure (12 weeks)
- Weeks 1–3 (Build the habit; aerobic base)
  - 2 sessions/week
  - Session A (Zone 2 steady): 12–15 min continuous mix:
    - 2 min march in place
    - 2 min shadow box
    - 2 min step-touch or lateral steps
    - 2 min low step-ups (if safe) or alternating knee drives
    - 2–3 min march in place
    - Keep RPE 4–5. Breathe through nose as much as possible.
  - Session B (Intro intervals): 12–15 min total
    - Warm-up 3 min easy
    - 6–8 rounds: 20s work / 40s easy
      - Work choices: mountain climbers (controlled), shadow boxing flurries, high-knee march, skaters (low).
      - Easy: march in place or step-touch.
    - Cool-down 2–3 min easy + breathing.

- Weeks 4–7 (Progress capacity; add threshold work)
  - 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A (Longer Zone 2): 16–20 min continuous at RPE 4–6. Rotate movements every 1–2 minutes to avoid monotony (march, shadow box, step-ups, low jacks, knee drives).
  - Session B (Threshold blocks): 16–18 min
    - Warm-up 3–4 min
    - 3 blocks x 3 min at RPE 7–8:
      - Example block: 45s high-knee march/run in place + 45s shadow box combos + 45s step-ups + 45s low-impact jacks.
    - 2 min easy between blocks.
  - Optional Session C (Power intervals or EMOM 12):
    - Option 1: 10 rounds 15s hard (RPE 8–9) + 45s easy.
    - Option 2: EMOM 12
      - Min 1: 20–25 controlled mountain climbers/leg
      - Min 2: 20–30 shadow boxing hard combos
      - Min 3: 12–15 squat-to-calf-raise
      - Scale to finish each minute with 10–15s spare.

- Weeks 8–12 (Consolidate; varied intensities)
  - 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A (Zone 2–3 steady): 18–25 min at RPE 4–6. Keep nasal breathing where possible; add occasional 20–30s pickups to RPE 7 every 3–4 minutes.
  - Session B (Tempo + intervals): 18–22 min
    - Warm-up 3–4 min
    - 2 x 4 min tempo at RPE 7 (e.g., brisk run-in-place + shadow box + step-ups), 2 min easy between.
    - Then 6 rounds 20s hard / 40s easy.
  - Optional Session C (Cardio-circuit finisher, 10–12 min) on a lifting day if you have time/energy:
    - Circuit, as many quality rounds as possible at RPE 6–7:
      - 30s shadow boxing
      - 30s marching/high-knee march
      - 30s step-outs or skaters (low)
      - 30s plank or dead bug for active recovery
      - 30–45s rest
    - Stop with 1–2 reps “in reserve” feeling—don’t empty the tank.

Warm-up template (3–5 min)
- 30s each: ankle rocks, hip circles, arm circles.
- 2 rounds of: 20s march in place, 20s step-touch, 20s shadow box easy.

Cool-down (2–4 min)
- Easy marching, then 1–2 minutes of 4-6 nasal breathing lying on the mat.
- Light calves/hip flexor stretch if tight.

Noise- and neighbor-friendly swaps
- Replace jumps with step-outs or squat-to-calf-raise.
- Use “invisible rope” instead of actual skipping.
- Emphasize quick hands (shadow boxing) and fast feet (march/run-in-place) over pounding the floor.
- Wear cushioned trainers; keep sessions on a rug/mat.

Progression rules
- Add 1–2 minutes to steady sessions when RPE stays ≤5.
- For intervals, first increase rounds, then shorten rest (e.g., 20/40 → 20/30), then increase work to 30s.
- Keep at least one Zone 2 session every week for recovery and aerobic base.
- If leg soreness is high from Bulgarians/squats, make cardio low-impact and keep RPE 4–5 that week.

Sample sessions you can copy-paste to your client
- 15-min Zone 2
  - 3 min march in place
  - 3 min shadow boxing
  - 3 min step-touch or lateral steps
  - 3 min alternating knee drives
  - 3 min march cool-down
- 16-min Intervals
  - Warm-up 3 min easy
  - 8 rounds: 20s skaters (low) + 40s march
  - Cool-down 1–2 min
- EMOM 12
  - Min 1: 20 push-up position shoulder taps (slow)
  - Min 2: 25–35 shadow boxing fast
  - Min 3: 16–20 alternating reverse lunges or step-backs (no impact)

Safety and recovery
- Stop if sharp pain, dizziness, or chest discomfort.
- Hydrate: extra 300–500 ml water if you sweat a lot.
- On high-stress weeks, drop to 1–2 shorter Zone 2 sessions and prioritize sleep.

This cardio plan will build aerobic fitness and conditioning without interfering with the 12-week strength program or requiring extra equipment or space.

Great question. With a small flat and a doorway bar, think compact, versatile, and incremental. Here’s a prioritized buy-list and why, plus budget tiers and how they’d plug into his current 12-week plan and beyond.

Top priorities (smallest footprint, biggest return)
1) A pair of adjustable dumbbells (ideal range 2–25 kg each)
- Why: Infinite exercise variety, easy progression, compact.
- What to look for:
  - Quick-change mechanism (spin-lock is cheaper but slower; selectable blocks are faster).
  - Minimum increment 1–2.5 kg per hand.
  - Knurled handle, plates that don’t rattle.
- Training impact:
  - Upper body: DB rows, Romanian deadlifts (RDL), floor press, shoulder press, curls, triceps extensions, weighted pull-up holds.
  - Lower body: Goblet squat, split squat/Bulgarian, RDL, calf raises.
  - Core: Weighted carries (in place), farmer hold, side bends, weighted hollow holds.
- Progression targets:
  - Goblet squat to 12–20 reps with 20–30 kg.
  - Single-arm row to 8–12 reps with 20–30 kg.
  - Floor press to 8–12 reps with 15–25 kg/hand.

2) A set of resistance bands (loop + handles)
- Why: Ultra-compact, adds load to push-ups/chin-ups, assistance for pull-ups, joint-friendly pumps/finishers.
- Get:
  - 3–4 continuous-loop bands: light, medium, heavy.
  - Optional tube band with door anchor and handles.
- Uses:
  - Assistance: band-assisted chin-ups while learning the concentric.
  - Overload: banded push-ups, RDLs with DB + band, face pulls, pull-aparts, rows.
  - Warm-ups, rehab, deload weeks.

3) Gymnastic rings (nylon straps) for the doorway bar or a beam
- Why: Huge strength and scapular control carryover; store flat.
- Uses:
  - Ring rows (perfect horizontal pulling before/alongside pull-ups).
  - Ring push-ups/dips (progression toward deeper ROM; dips later if safe).
  - Scap stability (support holds, Y-T-W variations).
- Note: Ensure mounting height and clearance; dips may require more space—start with rows and push-ups.

Nice-to-have next steps (still compact)
4) Adjustable kettlebell (or 12–24 kg fixed bells if space allows)
- Why: Excellent for hinges, conditioning, and unilateral strength.
- Uses:
  - Swings (hip power), goblet squats, cleans, presses, snatches (later), single-leg RDLs.
- If only one: pick 16 kg for general use; stronger trainees quickly benefit from 20–24 kg.

5) Weight belt or dip belt + small plates
- Why: Progress chin-ups/pull-ups once you can do 5–8 solid reps.
- Start with 2.5–5 kg added; microload over time.

6) Door anchor pad and protective floor tiles
- Why: Protects doorframes with bands; reduces noise and floor scuffing.

Space- and budget-conscious barbell alternative
7) Loadable dumbbell handles + standard plates (1", or Olympic 2")
- Why: Cheaper heavy loading than premium adjustable DBs; lets you reach 30–40+ kg per hand if needed.
- Use collars for safety; store plates under a bed/sofa.

If you have a bit more space
8) Foldable squat stand or wall-mounted rack + adjustable bench + barbell/plates
- Big jump in capability, but only if space and budget allow.
- Opens heavy squats, bench, deadlifts, hip thrusts. Not essential for great results, but highest ceiling long term.

Budget tiers
- Starter (<£75 | <$100)
  - Mixed loop bands set + door anchor
  - Ab wheel (optional) + yoga blocks for push-up depth
- Core kit (£150–£300 | $180–$350)
  - Adjustable dumbbells up to 20–25 kg each
  - Loop bands
  - Rings
- Expanded (£400–£700 | $500–$850)
  - Heavier adjustable DBs (up to 32–40 kg each) or loadable DB handles + plates
  - One adjustable kettlebell (16–24 kg)
  - Dip belt + small plates
- Premium compact (£800+ | $1,000+)
  - High-end selectorized DBs (e.g., up to 41–43 kg/90–95 lb each)
  - Fold-flat bench
  - Foldable rack if space permits

How this upgrades his current program
- Weeks 1–4: Keep bodyweight focus. Add light band assistance for chin-ups and banded push-up overload on final sets.
- Weeks 5–8: Introduce DB goblet squats, DB RDLs, DB rows, DB floor press. Use rings for ring rows and ring push-ups to deepen ROM.
- Weeks 9–12: Progress to Bulgarian split squats with DBs, weighted hip thrusts (DB on lap), feet-elevated ring push-ups, chin-up negatives with a small DB between feet or a belt if appropriate.

Example progression with just DBs + bands
- Lower body:
  - Goblet squat 3x8–12 → Bulgarian split squat 3–4x8–10 holding DBs → front-rack split squat with two DBs.
  - Hip hinge: Bodyweight bridge → DB hip thrusts 4x8–12 → single-leg RDL 3x8–10/side.
- Upper push:
  - Floor push-up → banded push-up → DB floor press 4x6–12 → ring push-up (harder ROM).
- Upper pull:
  - Assisted chin-up → band-assisted to unassisted → weighted chin-ups.
  - Ring rows → 1-arm DB row 4x8–12.

Quality and safety notes
- Doorway bar: Confirm load rating; rings must hang so the door can’t open toward you.
- Bands: Inspect for cracks; anchor with a towel to protect paint/edges.
- DBs/KBs: Clear a 2x2 m floor space; use a mat to dampen noise; keep a small step-stool or sofa for hip thrust setup.
- Microloading: Progress 1–2 reps first, then add the smallest load you can. For DBs without microplates, use fractional wrist weights (0.5–1 kg).

If buying just one item first
- Adjustable dumbbells win. They immediately expand the plan without requiring any layout change and will serve for years.

If noise/neighbor concerns are high
- Favor DBs, bands, and rings over kettlebell ballistic work at first; add swings later during daytime hours.

This path keeps his flat uncluttered while giving him clear, long-term progression in strength.

Got it. Here’s an intensified Phase 2 (Weeks 4–7) that preserves joint safety but drives harder stimulus via harder variations, top sets near failure, density work, and strategic overload on pulls and single-leg patterns. It still fits a mat + doorway bar setup. Use RIR targets to manage effort.

Global rules for Phase 2 (intensity focus)

Here’s a Saturday “Fun Finisher Day” that’s short, varied, and scalable in a small flat. It won’t wreck recovery but scratches the itch to move. Pick one of the formats each Saturday and rotate weekly. Session time: 15–25 minutes including warm-up and cool-down.

General rules
- Effort: RPE 6–8 (finish sweaty, not smashed). Keep 1–2 reps in reserve on any strength moves.
- Equipment: yoga mat, doorway bar, optional towel and chair.
- Warm-up (3–4 min): 30s each x2 rounds — march in place, arm circles, step-outs, shadow box easy.

Option 1: Bodyweight Game — 20-min Deck of Cards
- Assign suits:
  - Hearts = Push-ups (scale: incline or knee as needed)
  - Spades = Squats (tempo 3s down)
  - Diamonds = Alternating reverse lunges (each leg = 1 rep)
  - Clubs = Hollow rocks or dead bug (5 rocks = 1 “rep”)
- Card value = reps (Face = 10, Ace = 11; Jokers = 30s plank)
- Draw 1–2 cards at a time, work continuously for up to 20 min. Keep form crisp; rest as needed.

Option 2: Pull-up Party — EMOM 18
- Minute 1: Chin-up skill — 1–3 reps or 1 rep + 6–10s negative + 10–20s flexed-arm hang
- Minute 2: Push — 8–15 push-ups (feet-elevated if strong; incline if needed)
- Minute 3: Core/leg — 10–14 tempo squats (3s down + 1s pause) or 8–10 Bulgarian split squats/leg alternating weeks
- Goal: Finish each minute with ~10–15s to spare. Scale reps to stay smooth.

Option 3: Shadow Box + Strength Flow — 5 x 3-min Rounds (boxing timer vibe)
- Round structure (3 min on / 45s rest x5):
  - 60s shadow boxing (combos + footwork, moderate-hard)
  - 30s push-ups (steady pace)
  - 30s squats (steady pace)
  - 30s mountain climbers or knee drives
  - 30s breathing reset (march in place, nasal breathing)
- Keep the hands fast and feet light; no max-out.

Option 4: “Chipper” Circuit — Beat Your Time (cap 18–20 min)
- Complete in order; rest only as needed:
  - 40 bodyweight squats
  - 30 push-ups (scale as needed)
  - 20 alternating reverse lunges/leg (40 total)
  - 10 chin-ups (singles OK, assist as needed; count 2 slow negatives as 1 rep if necessary)
  - 60s hollow hold
- Record time. Next time, aim to match or beat with cleaner reps or fewer assists.

Option 5: Core + Grip Quest — 3 Rounds for Quality
- A1) Dead bug slow 8/side (3s lower)
- A2) Towel hang from pull-up bar 20–40s (loop a towel over the bar to challenge grip)
- A3) Side plank 25–40s/side
- A4) Hip thrust (shoulders on sofa) 12–15 with 2s squeeze
- Rest 60–75s between rounds. Finish with 2 sets of max-effort shadow boxing 45s on/30s off.

Option 6: “Ladder Fun” — 10-Min Push/Pull Ladder + 5-Min Leg Burner
- Push/Pull Ladder (10 min continuous):
  - 1 push-up + 1 chin-up (or 1 negative) → 2 + 2 → 3 + 3 … climb until form slows, then descend.
  - Scale: incline/knee push-ups; for pull, use assisted concentric or negatives.
- Leg Burner (5 min AMRAP):
  - 6 Bulgarian split squats/leg
  - 6 squat-to-calf-raises
  - 20s march/run in place
  - Keep moving, smooth reps.

Option 7: “Around the World” — 4 Stations x 3 Rounds (16–20 min)
- Station 1: 45s shadow boxing (power shots last 10s) → 15s rest
- Station 2: 45s push-ups (scale) → 15s rest
- Station 3: 45s squats or jump squats (submax, soft landings) → 15s rest
- Station 4: 45s hollow rocks or plank → 60s rest
- Repeat 3 rounds. Track reps, try to keep within ±2 reps across rounds for consistency.

Cool-down (2–3 min)
- Easy marching + 90/90 hip stretch + doorway chest stretch + 1–2 min nasal 4-6 breathing.

How to integrate with the week
- Keep Friday strength day normal.
- Saturday finisher at RPE 6–8.
- If legs are trashed from Bulgarians, choose an upper/core-biased option (2, 5, or 7). If elbows/shoulders are tender, pick lower-body/cardio emphasis (1 with more squats/lunges, 3 with fewer push-ups).
- If recovery dips, shorten to 12–15 min or skip that week.

Here’s a simple, efficient mobility routine you can give him. It fits a small flat, needs only the mat, and targets the areas most taxed by the program (ankles, hips, thoracic spine, shoulders, wrists). Use it as a 10–15 minute daily routine or a 6–8 minute condensed warm-up version before training. Include a slightly longer 20–25 minute session 1–2x/week for deeper work.

Daily mobility (10–15 minutes)
- Breath + reset (1 minute)
  - 90/90 breathing on back: feet on sofa or wall, knees/hips ~90°, one hand on belly, one on ribs. 4s inhale, 6s exhale x 6–8 breaths.
- Spine and shoulders (3–4 minutes)
  - Cat–cow: 8 slow reps (2s each direction).
  - Thread-the-needle: 6–8 reps/side (exhale as you reach under; optional 10s end-range hold on last rep).
  - Prone T/Y/Ws: 6 reps each (slow 2s lift, 2s lower) to wake up mid-back and shoulders.
- Hips (4–5 minutes)
  - 90/90 hip switches: 6–8 flowing reps each side; add 10–20s forward fold hold on tight side.
  - Hip flexor half-kneeling stretch: 30–45s/side; squeeze glute of the back leg and gently tuck pelvis.
  - Figure-4 glute stretch (on back): 30–45s/side; breathe slow.
- Ankles and calves (2–3 minutes)
  - Knee-to-wall ankle rocks: 12–15 reps/side, heel stays down.
  - Calf stretch against wall or step: 30–45s straight-knee, then 30–45s bent-knee/side.
- Chest and lats (2–3 minutes)
  - Doorway pec stretch: 30–45s/side at a mild–moderate stretch.
  - Lat stretch with counter/sofa: hands on edge, sit hips back, 30–45s; add side-bend breathing.

Condensed pre-lift warm-up mobility (6–8 minutes)
- 1 minute nasal breathing + rib expansion.
- 2 minutes flow: inchworms x5, world’s greatest stretch x3/side (lunge, elbow to instep, T-spine rotation), 10 bodyweight squats (2s down).
- 2 minutes shoulders: scapular pull-ups x6–8, band pull-aparts or prone Ts x10–12, arm circles x10 each.
- 2 minutes hips/ankles: 90/90 switches x6 total, knee-to-wall ankle rocks x10/side, 10 glute bridges.

Post-session cool-down (3–5 minutes)
- 90/90 breathing x 6–8 breaths.
- Hip flexor stretch 30–45s/side.
- Doorway pec stretch 30–45s/side.
- Gentle neck side-bends and rotations x5 each.

Weekly deep-dive (20–25 minutes, 1–2x/week)
- Breath + pelvic tuck (2 minutes)
  - Supine 90/90 breathing with light pelvic tilt; exhale fully to feel ribs down.
- Thoracic extension (3 minutes)
  - Over small pillow/rolled towel between shoulder blades: 3 x 30–45s holds, arms overhead.
  - Open books: 6–8 reps/side; pause 2s at end-range.
- Shoulders/scapula (4 minutes)
  - Wall slides: 2x10 slow reps.
  - Pike scapular shrugs: 2x10–12.
  - Sleeper stretch: 20–30s/side if posterior shoulder feels tight.
- Hips (6–8 minutes)
  - 90/90 stretch: 45–60s forward fold on front hip/side, 45–60s tall posture on back hip/side; switch sides.
  - Half-kneeling hip flexor + side-bend: 45–60s/side.
  - Adductor rock-backs (wide-knee child’s pose): 8–10 slow reps + 20–30s hold.
- Ankles/feet (3–4 minutes)
  - Knee-to-wall test and mobilization: 2x12 reps/side.
  - Toe extensor stretch (kneeling, sit back on toes) 20–30s; plantar fascia roll on a ball or fist 30–60s/foot.
- Neck and grip (2–3 minutes)
  - Neck controlled circles: 3 slow each direction.
  - Towel hangs from doorway bar: 2 x 20–30s for forearm tissue tolerance; keep shoulders packed.

Optional micro-mobility snacks (60–120 seconds, 1–3x/day)
- Desk shoulders: 10 band pull-aparts or 10 wall slides.
- Hips: 90/90 switches x8 or 30s couch/sofa hip flexor stretch per side.
- Ankles: 20 ankle rocks while the kettle boils.
- Spine: 5 open books or 30s thoracic extension over pillow.

Programming notes for this client
- Prioritize hips/ankles on heavy squat/Bulgarian days; prioritize thoracic/shoulders on pull-up/push-up emphasis days.
- Keep stretches at mild–moderate intensity; no numbness or pinching. Ease off if sharp pain.
- Breathe through the nose and exhale fully during end-range holds; aim for 4–6 slow breaths per stretch.
- Consistency beats intensity: 10 minutes daily will outperform 30 minutes once a week.

Progress checks (every 3–4 weeks)
- Ankle: Knee-to-wall distance (cm) without heel lift—aim to add 1–2 cm.
- Hips: 90/90 posture—can he sit taller and hinge further forward?
- Thoracic: Can he get both shoulders and elbows to the floor on open books without rib flare?
- Shoulders: Scapular control—more comfortable overhead reach and longer, stronger active hangs.

- Chin-up: 6–8 singles—attempt unassisted; follow misses with 1 negative (8–10s)
- Hollow hold 3x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat 3x8
- Pike push-up 3x6–8
- Flexed-arm hang 3x max
- Single-leg bridge 3x10–12
- Side plank 2x30–40s/side

Session C (light technique)
- Mobility flow + 2x8–10 easy squats + 2x6–8 easy push-ups + 4–6 assisted chin-up reps total; stay fresh.

Week 12 (Testing and consolidation)
Session A (Test)
- Max quality push-ups in one set (stop 1 rep before form breaks)
- Chin-ups: up to 6–8 singles; record best unassisted set OR best negative time and best flexed-arm hang
- Bulgarian split squat AMRAP/leg at clean tempo; stop 1–2 RIR (cap 20)
- Accessory: light hip thrust 2x12; core 2x30–40s

Session B (Volume back on)
- Squat 4x10
- Push-up 4x8–12 (feet-elevated as able)
- Chin-up 6x1–2 assisted + negative focus

Session C (Skill/capacity)
- EMOM 12: Odd 2–3 chin-ups (least assist); Even 6–10 push-ups (scaled)
- Cool-down and note progress

Saturday “Fun Finisher Day” (choose one each Saturday; 15–25 min)
- Option 1: Deck of Cards game (push-ups, squats, reverse lunges, hollow rocks; Jokers = 30s plank)
- Option 2: EMOM 18—Min1 chins/negatives/hang; Min2 push-ups; Min3 tempo squats or Bulgarians
- Option 3: 5 x 3-min boxing-style rounds (shadow box + push-ups + squats + climbers + easy march)
- Option 4: Chipper for time (40 squats, 30 push-ups, 40 lunges total, 10 chin-ups or 5 negatives, 60s hollow)
- Option 5: Core + Grip Quest—3 rounds quality: dead bug, towel hang, side plank, hip thrust; finish with 2x45s shadow box sprints
- Option 6: Push/Pull Ladder 10 min + 5-min leg burner
- Option 7: 4-station circuit x3 rounds (shadow box, push-ups, squats/jump squats, hollow/plank)

Home cardio plan (2–3x/week, 10–25 min)
- Weeks 1–3: 2 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2: 12–15 min continuous mix (march, shadow box, step-touch, knee drives), RPE 4–5
  - Session B Intervals: 6–8 rounds 20s work/40s easy (mountain climbers, skaters, high-knee march), total 12–15 min
- Weeks 4–7: 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2: 16–20 min, RPE 4–6
  - Session B Threshold blocks: 3 x 3 min at RPE 7–8; 2 min easy between
  - Optional Session C: Power intervals 10 x 15s hard/45s easy or EMOM 12 (climbers, shadow box, squat-to-calf-raise)
- Weeks 8–12: 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2–3: 18–25 min, add 20–30s pickups to RPE 7 every 3–4 min
  - Session B Tempo + intervals: 2 x 4 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy; then 6 x 20s hard/40s easy
  - Optional Session C finisher on a lift day: 10–12 min circuit at RPE 6–7
- Keep one easy Zone 2 weekly. If legs are sore from Bulgarians/squats, pick low-impact options and RPE 4–5.

Mobility routine
- Daily mobility (10–15 min)
  - 90/90 breathing x 6–8 breaths
  - Cat–cow x8; thread-the-needle 6–8/side; prone T/Y/W 6 each
  - 90/90 hip switches 6–8/side with 10–20s holds; half-kneeling hip flexor 30–45s/side; figure-4 glute 30–45s/side
  - Knee-to-wall ankle rocks 12–15/side; calf stretch straight and bent knee 30–45s/side
  - Doorway pec stretch 30–45s/side; lat stretch on counter/sofa 30–45s
- Condensed pre-lift mobility (6–8 min)
  - 1 min nasal breathing; inchworms x5; world’s greatest stretch x3/side; 10 bodyweight squats
  - Scapular pull-ups x6–8; prone Ts x10–12; arm circles x10 each
  - 90/90 switches x6 total; knee-to-wall x10/side; 10 glute bridges
- Post-session (3–5 min): 90/90 breaths; hip flexor 30–45s/side; doorway pec 30–45s/side; gentle neck moves
- Weekly deep-dive (20–25 min, 1–2x/week): thoracic extension over pillow; open books; wall slides; pike scap shrugs; 90/90 long holds; hip flexor + side-bend; adductor rock-backs; ankle rocks; toe extensor stretch; towel hangs for grip.

Nutrition plan (for strength and recovery)
- Calories
  - Start at bodyweight (lb) x 15 kcal; if BW unknown, 2,400–2,800 kcal/day for average 27-year-old male.
  - Adjust by 150–250 kcal every 1–2 weeks based on 2-week weight average:
    - <0.25% BW/week gain: +150–250 kcal/day
    - >0.5% BW/week gain or sluggish: −150–250 kcal/day
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g/lb (1.8–2.2 g/kg) daily
- Fat: 25–35% of calories (≥0.3 g/kg)
- Carbs: remainder; bias around training
- Timing
  - 60–120 min pre: protein + carbs, low fat/fiber (e.g., yogurt + banana; oats + whey)
  - 0–2 h post: protein + carbs (e.g., rice + eggs; pasta + chicken; smoothie)
  - Evenly split protein 3–5 feedings of 25–45 g each
- Plate method (no tracking)
  - Training days: 1–2 palms protein; 2 cupped-hand carbs; 1–2 thumbs fats; 1–2 fists veg/fruit per meal
  - Rest days: same protein; 1–1.5 cupped-hand carbs; 1–2 thumbs fats; 1–2 fists veg/fruit
- Grocery list: eggs, Greek yogurt, milk, cottage cheese, whey, chicken thighs, tinned fish, mince, tofu/tempeh, lentils/beans; oats, rice, pasta, potatoes, wraps/bread, fruit/frozen fruit, cereal; olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocado; mixed veg/frozen; spices/sauces
- Sample 7-day menu: provided in prior message; rotate freely
- Macro examples
  - ~150 lb: 2,300–2,500 kcal; P 120–160 g; F 65–80 g; C 260–330 g
  - ~180 lb: 2,600–2,900 kcal; P 140–180 g; F 75–95 g; C 310–380 g
  - ~210 lb: 2,900–3,300 kcal; P 160–210 g; F 85–105 g; C 350–430 g
- Supplements (optional)
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day
  - Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU/day if low sun (check with clinician)
  - Omega-3 1–2 g EPA/DHA if fish <2x/week
  - Whey/casein to hit protein; caffeine 100–200 mg pre if desired
- Habits
  - Batch-cook; build meals protein-first; keep quick options; 20% fun foods; eat to 80–90% fullness; limit alcohol 0–4 drinks/week
- Monitor
  - Weigh 3–4 mornings/week; 2-week rolling average
  - If performance and recovery stall and weight is flat, +150–250 kcal/day
  - Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L water/day; +500 ml around training; salt food to taste

Equipment roadmap (optional for later)
- First buy: adjustable dumbbells (to 20–25 kg each), loop bands, and optionally rings.
- Progressions with DBs: goblet/Bulgarian squats, DB RDLs, DB rows, DB floor press, loaded hip thrusts, weighted chins later.

Safety and setup
- Doorway bar: install per manufacturer; test with hangs first.
- Assistance for chins: foot on chair lightly; avoid kipping; control negatives.
- Floor: use mat/towel for knees and hamstring slides; keep 2x2 m area clear.
- Pain: stop if sharp/joint pain; regress and monitor.

Expected outcomes by Week 12 (typical adherence)
- Push-ups: move from incline/knee to 10–20+ strict floor reps; possibly 5–10 feet-elevated.
- Pull-ups: first 1–3 unassisted chin-ups or much longer hangs and slower negatives.
- Legs: strong, stable 8–12/leg Bulgarians with pauses; improved hinge strength.
- Core: 30–45s hollow holds and solid bracing in all movements.

This is your master 12-week package. Share weekly goals, RIR guidance, and Saturday options with your client, and adjust reps/variations based on recovery and progress.

Below is the complete 12-week program integrating all adjustments: intensified Phase 2, the Saturday fun finisher options, cardio plan, mobility routine, and the full nutrition plan. It’s organized by phases with week-by-week training, plus separate sections you can paste to your client for cardio, Saturday finisher choices, mobility, and nutrition.

Structure and global guidelines
- Strength frequency: 3 sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri), 40–60 min.
- Saturday: optional “Fun Finisher Day” (15–25 min).
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions/week, 10–25 min, on non-lifting or light days.
- Warm-up each strength session (5–8 min): joint prep, dynamic, activation:
  - Neck circles x5 each; shoulder CARs x5 each; hip CARs x3 each
  - Leg swings x10 each; arm circles x10 each; inchworms x5; hip hinge drill x10
  - Activation: scapular pull-ups x6–8; glute bridge x12; dead bug x6/side
- Cool-down after strength (3–5 min): easy breathing + 90/90 hip stretch + doorway chest stretch + child’s pose or T-spine rotations.
- Tempo notation example: 3-1-1 = 3s lower, 1s pause, 1s up.
- Rest: 60–120s for big movements; 45–90s accessories/core.
- RIR: keep 1–2 reps in reserve on most sets unless noted for top-set efforts in Phase 2.

Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Learn movement patterns, build base strength, control tempo.

Week 1
Session A
- Squat to box/chair: 3x10, 3-1-1, rest 60–90s
- Incline push-up (hands on counter/sofa): 4x6–8, 3-1-1, 90s
- Assisted chin-up or negatives: 5x3 negatives (4–5s) or 4x6 assisted, 90–120s
- Hip bridge: 3x12–15, 2-1-2
- Dead bug: 3x6/side slow
- Scapular pull-ups: 2x8–10

Session B
- Split squat (light wall support): 3x8/leg, 3-1-1
- Knee push-up: 4x8–10, 2-1-1
- Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar): 4x max (10–20s target) or 4x3–4 eccentrics
- Hip thrust (shoulders on sofa): 3x10–12, 2-1-2
- Side plank: 3x20–30s/side
- Reverse snow angels: 2x10–12

Session C
- Tempo bodyweight squat: 4x8, 4-1-1
- Incline push-up: 4x8–10, 2-1-1
- Assisted neutral/supinated chin-ups: 5x3–4 negatives or 4x6 assisted
- Hamstring walkouts: 3x6–8 slow
- Hollow hold (tucked if needed): 4x15–25s
- Pike scapular shrugs: 2x10–12

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps/set or 1 set if you finish with ≥2 RIR across sets.
- Add 1s pause at bottom of squats/push-ups.
- Chin-ups: extend negatives to 5–6s; add 1–2s to hangs.

Week 3
- Push-ups: lower hand height or introduce 1–2 sets of full push-ups for 4–6 reps if ready.
- Squats: +1–2 reps/set or add 2s pause on some reps.
- Chin-ups: combine 1–2 assisted concentrics + 1–2 slow negatives per set.
- Core: Hollow hold 20–35s; side plank 30–40s.

Optional conditioning (Weeks 1–3, 1–2x/week, 10–15 min)
- EMOM 10: 6–8 incline/knee push-ups (min 1), 8–10 squats (min 2). Keep 2–3 RIR.

Phase 2: Intensified Strength (Weeks 4–7)
Goal: Harder variations, top-set intensity, density work; strong pull-up progress.

Global for Phase 2
- One top set at 0–1 RIR for main push and squat pattern each session; rest 90–150s for main lifts.
- Controlled eccentrics (3–4s) and 1–2s pauses as prescribed.
- Pull-ups twice per week minimum with long negatives (6–10s) and isometric holds.

Week 4
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa) 4x6–8/leg, 2s pause; last set AMRAP 0–1 RIR
- Push-up (feet elevated 10–20 cm if ≥10 floor reps) 5x6–10; last set AMRAP 0–1 RIR
- Chin-up cluster x7 rounds: 1 assisted concentric + 1 negative (6–8s) + 3s mid-range iso; 60–75s
- Hip thrust (sofa) 4x10–12; final set AMRAP 1 RIR
- Hollow hold 4x25–35s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x8–10, 4-1-1; last set AMRAP ~1 RIR
- Pike push-up 5x5–9 (elevate feet if strong); last set AMRAP 0–1 RIR
- Flexed-arm hang 5x max (aim 20–30s); then 2x1 slow negatives (8–10s)
- Hamstring walkouts 4x8–10 slow, 2s stretch end range
- Side plank with top-leg raise 3x25–35s/side

Session C
- Split squat (front foot on book 2–4 cm) 4x8–10/leg, 3s eccentric
- Push-up density: 5 rounds 40s work/20s rest; accumulate reps
- Chin-up EMOM 10: Odd min 2 assisted reps + 1 6–8s negative; Even min 1–2 attempts
- Single-leg glute bridge 3x12–15/leg (2s squeeze)
- Hollow rocks 3x10–15

Week 5
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 5x6–9/leg; top set AMRAP 0–1 RIR; back-off 2x8 (2 RIR)
- Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–10; last set AMRAP
- Chin-up cluster x8 rounds; negatives 8–10s
- Hip thrust 4x12–15; last set AMRAP 1 RIR
- Hollow hold 4x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x10 (4-0-1); last set AMRAP 1 RIR
- Pike push-up 5x6–10; last set AMRAP; add 2–3s eccentric on final 2 reps
- Flexed-arm hang 5x max; then scapular pull-ups 2x12–15
- Hamstring walkouts 4x10–12
- Side plank 3x30–45s/side

Session C
- Split squat 4x10/leg, 3s eccentric + 1s pause
- Push-up density: 6 rounds 40s on/20s off; target +5–10% total reps vs Week 4
- Chin-up EMOM 10–12
- Single-leg bridge 3x15/leg
- Hollow rocks 3x12–16

Week 6
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 5x6–8/leg, 2s pause; top set AMRAP 0–1 RIR
- Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–10; add 2s pause at bottom for first 3 reps each set
- Chin-up isometric overload: 5 sets—10–15s mid-range hold + 1 negative (8–10s), 120s rest
- Hip thrust 4x12–15; last set AMRAP
- Hollow hold 4x35–45s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x8–10 (4-1-1); last set AMRAP
- Pike push-up 5x6–9 with 3s eccentric; last set AMRAP
- Flexed-arm hang 4x max + 1–2 negatives (10s)
- Hamstring walkouts 4x10–12 (2s end-range)
- Side plank with reach-through 3x30–40s/side

Session C
- Bulgarian split squat reverse ladder: 8,8,7,7,6/leg (60–75s rest)
- Push-up cluster: 6 rounds—2–4 reps every 30–40s feet-elevated; finish with 1 floor AMRAP
- Chin-up density: 9 min on-the-minute 1 attempt + 1 negative; increase negatives/partials quality
- Single-leg bridge 3x12–15
- Hollow rocks 3x12–18

Week 7 (Density week—cut rests ~15–20%, maintain quality)
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 5x6–9/leg; shorter rest; last set AMRAP
- Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–10; shorter rest; last set AMRAP
- Chin-up EMOM 12: 1 attempt + 1 8–10s negative each minute
- Hip thrust 4x12–15; last set AMRAP
- Hollow hold 4x30–45s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x10; shorter rest; last set AMRAP
- Pike push-up 5x6–9; shorter rest; last set AMRAP
- Flexed-arm hang 4x max; finish with 2x1 10s negatives
- Hamstring walkouts 3x10–12
- Side plank 3x30–45s

Session C
- Push-up density finisher: 8 rounds 30s on/15s off; record total reps
- Split squat 4x8–10/leg, 3s eccentric; tight rest
- Chin-up cluster 6–7 rounds: 1 assisted concentric + 1 long negative + 5s top hold
- Single-leg bridge 3x12–15
- Hollow rocks 3x12–18

Phase 3: Consolidation, Skill Peaks, and Testing (Weeks 8–12)
Goal: Solidify gains, attempt first unassisted chin-ups, push harder push-up variations, stable unilateral legs, refine core.

Week 8
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 5x6–8/leg (2s pause)
- Push-up 5x8–12 or 4x5–8 feet-elevated + 1 back-off AMRAP (1 RIR)
- Chin-up wave sets: 5–6 rounds—1 assisted concentric + 1–2 negatives (6–8s) + 10–20s hold
- Hip thrust 4x12–15
- Hollow hold 4x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x10 (4-0-1)
- Pike push-up 5x6–10 (elevated feet if strong)
- Flexed-arm hang 5x max; then scapular pull-ups 2x12–15
- Single-leg bridge 4x12–15/leg
- Side plank 3x30–45s/side
- Reverse snow angels 2x15–20

Session C
- Squats 3x10, then 3x5 submax jump squats (crisp/soft landings)
- Push-up ladder: 5x submax sets, 1–2 RIR; total 40–60 reps target
- Chin-up attempts: 6–8 singles; then 2x1 slow negative (8s)
- Hamstring walkouts 3x10–12
- Hollow rocks 3x12–15

Week 9
- Feet-elevated push-ups for most sets; aim 6–10 reps.
- Chin-up: 8–10 singles across session; band/foot assist as needed; negatives 8–10s.
- Bulgarians: 5x8–10/leg as able.
- Optional finisher: EMOM 10 alternating 2–3 assisted chins and 6–8 push-ups.

Week 10
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 5x8–10/leg
- Feet-elevated push-up 5x6–10
- Chin-up cluster 6–8 rounds—attempt 1 unassisted; if fail, 1 assisted + 1 negative (8–10s)
- Hip thrust 4x12–15 (last set AMRAP, 1 RIR)
- Hollow hold 4x35–45s

Session B
- Tempo squat 4x10, 4-1-1
- Pike push-up (elevated feet if strong) 5x6–9
- Flexed-arm hang 5x max; aim 25–35s
- Single-leg bridge 4x12–15
- Side plank with top-leg raise 3x25–35s/side

Session C
- Squat density: 5 rounds—45s work/45s rest; smooth reps
- Push-up ladder to 50–70 total reps (include feet-elevated early sets)
- Chin-up EMOM 8: 1 attempt + 1 negative each minute

Week 11 (Taper and skill emphasis; -25% total sets)
Session A
- Bulgarian split squat 3x6–8/leg (quality)
- Feet-elevated push-up 3x6–10
- Chin-up: 6–8 singles—attempt unassisted; follow misses with 1 negative (8–10s)
- Hollow hold 3x30–40s

Session B
- Tempo squat 3x8
- Pike push-up 3x6–8
- Flexed-arm hang 3x max
- Single-leg bridge 3x10–12
- Side plank 2x30–40s/side

Session C (light technique)
- Mobility flow + 2x8–10 easy squats + 2x6–8 easy push-ups + 4–6 assisted chin-up reps total; stay fresh.

Week 12 (Testing and consolidation)
Session A (Test)
- Max quality push-ups in one set (stop 1 rep before form breaks)
- Chin-ups: up to 6–8 singles; record best unassisted set OR best negative time and best flexed-arm hang
- Bulgarian split squat AMRAP/leg at clean tempo; stop 1–2 RIR (cap 20)
- Accessory: light hip thrust 2x12; core 2x30–40s

Session B (Volume back on)
- Squat 4x10
- Push-up 4x8–12 (feet-elevated as able)
- Chin-up 6x1–2 assisted + negative focus

Session C (Skill/capacity)
- EMOM 12: Odd 2–3 chin-ups (least assist); Even 6–10 push-ups (scaled)
- Cool-down and note progress

Saturday “Fun Finisher Day” (choose one each Saturday; 15–25 min)
- Option 1: Deck of Cards game (push-ups, squats, reverse lunges, hollow rocks; Jokers = 30s plank)
- Option 2: EMOM 18—Min1 chins/negatives/hang; Min2 push-ups; Min3 tempo squats or Bulgarians
- Option 3: 5 x 3-min boxing-style rounds (shadow box + push-ups + squats + climbers + easy march)
- Option 4: Chipper for time (40 squats, 30 push-ups, 40 lunges total, 10 chin-ups or 5 negatives, 60s hollow)
- Option 5: Core + Grip Quest—3 rounds quality: dead bug, towel hang, side plank, hip thrust; finish with 2x45s shadow box sprints
- Option 6: Push/Pull Ladder 10 min + 5-min leg burner
- Option 7: 4-station circuit x3 rounds (shadow box, push-ups, squats/jump squats, hollow/plank)

Home cardio plan (2–3x/week, 10–25 min)
- Weeks 1–3: 2 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2: 12–15 min continuous mix (march, shadow box, step-touch, knee drives), RPE 4–5
  - Session B Intervals: 6–8 rounds 20s work/40s easy (mountain climbers, skaters, high-knee march), total 12–15 min
- Weeks 4–7: 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2: 16–20 min, RPE 4–6
  - Session B Threshold blocks: 3 x 3 min at RPE 7–8; 2 min easy between
  - Optional Session C: Power intervals 10 x 15s hard/45s easy or EMOM 12 (climbers, shadow box, squat-to-calf-raise)
- Weeks 8–12: 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session A Zone 2–3: 18–25 min, add 20–30s pickups to RPE 7 every 3–4 min
  - Session B Tempo + intervals: 2 x 4 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy; then 6 x 20s hard/40s easy
  - Optional Session C finisher on a lift day: 10–12 min circuit at RPE 6–7
- Keep one easy Zone 2 weekly. If legs are sore from Bulgarians/squats, pick low-impact options and RPE 4–5.

Mobility routine
- Daily mobility (10–15 min)
  - 90/90 breathing x 6–8 breaths
  - Cat–cow x8; thread-the-needle 6–8/side; prone T/Y/W 6 each
  - 90/90 hip switches 6–8/side with 10–20s holds; half-kneeling hip flexor 30–45s/side; figure-4 glute 30–45s/side
  - Knee-to-wall ankle rocks 12–15/side; calf stretch straight and bent knee 30–45s/side
  - Doorway pec stretch 30–45s/side; lat stretch on counter/sofa 30–45s
- Condensed pre-lift mobility (6–8 min)
  - 1 min nasal breathing; inchworms x5; world’s greatest stretch x3/side; 10 bodyweight squats
  - Scapular pull-ups x6–8; prone Ts x10–12; arm circles x10 each
  - 90/90 switches x6 total; knee-to-wall x10/side; 10 glute bridges
- Post-session (3–5 min): 90/90 breaths; hip flexor 30–45s/side; doorway pec 30–45s/side; gentle neck moves
- Weekly deep-dive (20–25 min, 1–2x/week): thoracic extension over pillow; open books; wall slides; pike scap shrugs; 90/90 long holds; hip flexor + side-bend; adductor rock-backs; ankle rocks; toe extensor stretch; towel hangs for grip.

Nutrition plan (for strength and recovery)
- Calories
  - Start at bodyweight (lb) x 15 kcal; if BW unknown, 2,400–2,800 kcal/day for average 27-year-old male.
  - Adjust by 150–250 kcal every 1–2 weeks based on 2-week weight average:
    - <0.25% BW/week gain: +150–250 kcal/day
    - >0.5% BW/week gain or sluggish: −150–250 kcal/day
- Protein: 0.8–1.0 g/lb (1.8–2.2 g/kg) daily
- Fat: 25–35% of calories (≥0.3 g/kg)
- Carbs: remainder; bias around training
- Timing
  - 60–120 min pre: protein + carbs, low fat/fiber (e.g., yogurt + banana; oats + whey)
  - 0–2 h post: protein + carbs (e.g., rice + eggs; pasta + chicken; smoothie)
  - Evenly split protein 3–5 feedings of 25–45 g each
- Plate method (no tracking)
  - Training days: 1–2 palms protein; 2 cupped-hand carbs; 1–2 thumbs fats; 1–2 fists veg/fruit per meal
  - Rest days: same protein; 1–1.5 cupped-hand carbs; 1–2 thumbs fats; 1–2 fists veg/fruit
- Grocery list: eggs, Greek yogurt, milk, cottage cheese, whey, chicken thighs, tinned fish, mince, tofu/tempeh, lentils/beans; oats, rice, pasta, potatoes, wraps/bread, fruit/frozen fruit, cereal; olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocado; mixed veg/frozen; spices/sauces
- Sample 7-day menu: provided in prior message; rotate freely
- Macro examples
  - ~150 lb: 2,300–2,500 kcal; P 120–160 g; F 65–80 g; C 260–330 g
  - ~180 lb: 2,600–2,900 kcal; P 140–180 g; F 75–95 g; C 310–380 g
  - ~210 lb: 2,900–3,300 kcal; P 160–210 g; F 85–105 g; C 350–430 g
- Supplements (optional)
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day
  - Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU/day if low sun (check with clinician)
  - Omega-3 1–2 g EPA/DHA if fish <2x/week
  - Whey/casein to hit protein; caffeine 100–200 mg pre if desired
- Habits
  - Batch-cook; build meals protein-first; keep quick options; 20% fun foods; eat to 80–90% fullness; limit alcohol 0–4 drinks/week
- Monitor
  - Weigh 3–4 mornings/week; 2-week rolling average
  - If performance and recovery stall and weight is flat, +150–250 kcal/day
  - Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L water/day; +500 ml around training; salt food to taste

Equipment roadmap (optional for later)
- First buy: adjustable dumbbells (to 20–25 kg each), loop bands, and optionally rings.
- Progressions with DBs: goblet/Bulgarian squats, DB RDLs, DB rows, DB floor press, loaded hip thrusts, weighted chins later.

Safety and setup
- Doorway bar: install per manufacturer; test with hangs first.
- Assistance for chins: foot on chair lightly; avoid kipping; control negatives.
- Floor: use mat/towel for knees and hamstring slides; keep 2x2 m area clear.
- Pain: stop if sharp/joint pain; regress and monitor.

Expected outcomes by Week 12 (typical adherence)
- Push-ups: move from incline/knee to 10–20+ strict floor reps; possibly 5–10 feet-elevated.
- Pull-ups: first 1–3 unassisted chin-ups or much longer hangs and slower negatives.
- Legs: strong, stable 8–12/leg Bulgarians with pauses; improved hinge strength.
- Core: 30–45s hollow holds and solid bracing in all movements.

This is your master 12-week package. Share weekly goals, RIR guidance, and Saturday options with your client, and adjust reps/variations based on recovery and progress.
